root_cause: The daily autonomous engineering optimizer tuned from queue, execution, cancellations and failures, but ignored workflow fan-out and skipped-job waste. It could therefore increase parallelism even while orchestration fan-out remained unnecessarily high.
prevention_rule: Daily tuning must include workflow fan-out p95 and skipped-job ratio. High fan-out or skip waste reduces parallelism and increases batching. Safe parallelism may increase only when queue, failure, fan-out and skip pressure are all low. Observations remain telemetry and are never persisted as tuning fields.

evidence.safety: Persistent tuning remains bounded to existing safe tuning fields and mandatory safety booleans.
